The Yobe State Council of the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has issued a 14-day ultimatum to the state government to address three key welfare demands or risk industrial action.
The ultimatum, which took effect on October 28, 2026, expires at midnight on November 11. The union’s position was contained in a statement signed by its state chairman, Comrade Ali Usman.
Among its demands is the implementation of the 65-year retirement age for non-academic staff in state-owned tertiary institutions.
The union is also demanding the immediate implementation of the reviewed 2024 salary table under the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Salary Structure (CONTEDISS), as well as the approval and implementation of the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA) and applicable Earned Allowance (EA).
The NASU expressed dissatisfaction with what it described as unequal treatment of academic and non-academic staff, noting that the state government had approved the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) for academic staff, while similar proposals submitted jointly under the Joint Academic and Non-Academic Staff Union (JANASU) on behalf of non-academic personnel remained unattended to.
While acknowledging the contributions of lecturers to the development of tertiary institutions, the union said non-academic staff also played critical roles in the administrative, technical and operational activities necessary for the effective running of the institutions.
It argued that the failure to give non-academic staff equal consideration could undermine institutional efficiency and harmonious industrial relations.
The statement added that the prolonged delay in addressing the demands had generated widespread dissatisfaction among members and negatively affected staff morale across the affected institutions.
The union urged the state government to use the 14-day ultimatum to take concrete steps towards resolving the issues, warning that failure to meet the demands by November 11 would prompt its leadership to reconvene on November 12 to determine the next line of action in accordance with labour laws.
It appealed to Governor Mai Mala Buni and other relevant government stakeholders to intervene and address the demands to avert industrial unrest and possible disruption of academic and administrative activities in the state’s tertiary institutions.
